text: In a triangle PQR, the co-ordinates of the points P and Q are ($-$2, 4) and (4, $-$2) respectively. If the equation of the perpendicular bisector of PR is 2x $-$ y + 2 = 0, then the centre of the circumcircle of the $\Delta$PQR is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Mid point of $PQ\equiv \left (\frac{-2+4}{2},\frac{4-2}{2}\right )\equiv (1,1)$

Slope of $PQ=\frac{4+2}{-2-4}=-1$

Slope of perpendicular bisector of PQ = 1

Equation of perpendicular bisector of PQ 

$y-1=1(x-1)$

$\Rightarrow y=x$

Solving with perpendicular bisector of PR,

2x $-$ y + 2 = 0

Circumcentre is ($-$2, $-$2)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift

text:
Which of the following statements is correct for the function g($α$) for $α$ $\in$ R such that 

$g(α)=\int\limits _{\frac{π}{6}}^{\frac{π}{3}}\frac{\sin ^{α}x}{\cos ^{α}x+\sin ^{α}x}dx$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$g(α)=\int\limits _{π/6}^{π/3}\frac{\sin ^{α}\left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )}{\cos ^{α}\left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )+\sin ^{α}\left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )}dx$

$=\int\limits _{π/6}^{π/3}\frac{\cos ^{α}x}{\sin ^{α}x+\cos ^{α}x}dx$

$\therefore$ $2.g(α)=\int\limits _{π/6}^{π/3}\frac{\sin ^{α}x+\cos ^{α}x}{\sin ^{α}x+\cos ^{α}x}dx=\int\limits _{π/6}^{π/3}dx=\frac{π}{3}-\frac{π}{6}=\frac{π}{6}$

$\Rightarrow$ $g(α)=\frac{π}{12}$ i.e. a constant function hence an even function.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift

text:
Which of the following is true for y(x) that satisfies the differential equation 

$\frac{dy}{dx}$ = xy $-$ 1 + x $-$ y; y(0) = 0 :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=(x-1)y+(x-1)$

$\frac{dy}{dx}=(x-1)(y+1)$

$\frac{dy}{y+1}=(x-1)dx$

Integrating both sides, we get

$\ln (y+1)=\frac{x^{2}}{2}-x+c$

$x=0,y=0$

$\Rightarrow c=0$

$\therefore$ $\ln (y+1)=\frac{x^{2}}{2}-x$

putting $x=1,\ln (y+1)=\frac{1}{2}-1=-\frac{1}{2}$

$y+1=e^{-\frac{1}{2}}$

$y=e^{-\frac{1}{2}}-1$

$\therefore$ $y(1)=e^{-\frac{1}{2}}-1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift

text:
The sum of possible values of x for 

$\tan ^{-1}(x + 1) + \cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{x-1}\right )$ $= \tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{8}{31}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The term $\cot ^{-1}\dfrac{1}{x-1}$ needs $x\neq 1$, and $\tan ^{-1}\dfrac{8}{31}<\dfrac{π}{4}$.

For $x>1$: $\cot ^{-1}\dfrac{1}{x-1}=\tan ^{-1}(x-1)>0$ and $\tan ^{-1}(x+1)>\tan ^{-1}2>\dfrac{π}{4}$, so the left side exceeds the right side and there is no solution.

For $x<1$: $\dfrac{1}{x-1}<0$, so $\cot ^{-1}\dfrac{1}{x-1}=π+\tan ^{-1}(x-1)$ and the equation becomes

$\tan ^{-1}(x+1)+\tan ^{-1}(x-1)=\tan ^{-1}\frac{8}{31}-π.$

The right side lies in $\left (-π,-\dfrac{π}{2}\right )$, which requires $x+1<0$, $x-1<0$ and $(x+1)(x-1)>1$, that is $x<-1$ and $x^{2}>2$.

Taking the tangent of both sides:

$\frac{(x+1)+(x-1)}{1-(x^{2}-1)}=\frac{8}{31}\Rightarrow \frac{2x}{2-x^{2}}=\frac{8}{31}\Rightarrow 4x^{2}+31x-8=0\Rightarrow (x+8)(4x-1)=0.$

Only $x=-8$ satisfies $x<-1$, $x^{2}>2$; indeed $\tan ^{-1}(-7)+\tan ^{-1}(-9)=-π+\tan ^{-1}\dfrac{-16}{1-63}=\tan ^{-1}\dfrac{8}{31}-π$.

At $x=\dfrac{1}{4}$ the left side is $\tan ^{-1}\dfrac{5}{4}+π-\tan ^{-1}\dfrac{3}{4}>π$, so $x=\dfrac{1}{4}$ is not a solution.

The sum of the possible values is $-8=-\dfrac{32}{4}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift

text: The inverse of $y=5^{\log x}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$y=5^{\log x}$

$\Rightarrow \log y=\log x.\log 5$

$\Rightarrow \log x=\frac{\log y}{\log 5}=\log _{5}y$

$\Rightarrow x=e^{\log _{5}y}$

$\Rightarrow x=y^{\log _{5}e}$

$\Rightarrow x=y^{\frac{1}{\log 5}}$

text: The system of equations kx + y + z = 1, x + ky + z = k and $x + y + zk = k^{2}$ has no solution if k is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$D=\left |\begin{array}{lll} k & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & k & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & k \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow k(k^{2}-1)-(k-1)+(1-k)=0$

$\Rightarrow (k-1)(k^{2}+k-1-1)=0$

$\Rightarrow (k-1)(k^{2}+k-2)=0$

$\Rightarrow (k-1)(k-1)(k+2)=0$

$\Rightarrow k=1,k=-2$

for k = 1 equation identical so k = $-$2 for no solution.

text: Team 'A' consists of 7 boys and n girls and Team 'B' has 4 boys and 6 girls. If a total of 52 single matches can be arranged between these two teams when a boy plays against a boy and a girl plays against a girl, then n is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

Total matches between boys of both team = ${}^{7}C_{1}\times {}^{4}C_{1}=28$

Total matches between girls of both team = ${}^{n}C_{1}{}^{6}C_{1}=6n$

Now, 28 + 6n = 52

$\Rightarrow$ n = 4

text:
Let there be three independent events $E_{1}, E_{2}$ and $E_{3}$. The probability that only $E_{1}$ occurs is $α$, only $E_{2}$ occurs is $β$ and only $E_{3}$ occurs is $γ$. Let 'p' denote the probability of none of events occurs that satisfies the equations 
($α$ $-$ 2$β$)p = $αβ$ and ($β$ $-$ 3$γ$)p = 2$βγ$. All the given probabilities are assumed to lie in the interval (0, 1).

Then, $\frac{ProbabilityofoccurrenceofE_{1}}{ProbabilityofoccurrenceofE_{3}}$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $P(E_{1}) = x, P(E_{2}) = y$ and $P(E_{3}) = z$

$α$ = P$\left (E_{1}\cap E–_{2}\cap E–_{3}\right )$ = $P(E_{1}).P\left (E–_{2}\right ).P\left (E–_{3}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = x(1 $-$ y) (1 $-$ z)  ......(i)

Similarly

β = (1 – x).y(1 – z) ...(ii)

$γ$ = (1 – x)(1 – y).z ...(iii)

p = (1 – x)(1 – y)(1 – z) ...(iv)

From (i) and (iv)

$\frac{x}{1-x}=\frac{α}{p}$

$\Rightarrow$ x = $\frac{α}{α+p}$

From (iii) and (iv)

$\frac{z}{1-z}=\frac{γ}{p}$

$\Rightarrow$ z = $\frac{γ}{γ+p}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{P(E_{1})}{P(E_{3})}=\frac{x}{z}=\frac{\frac{α}{α+p}}{\frac{γ}{γ+p}}$ $=\frac{\frac{γ+p}{γ}}{\frac{α+p}{α}}=\frac{1+\frac{p}{γ}}{1+\frac{p}{α}}$ ..(v)

Also given,

($α$ $-$ 2$β$)p = $αβ$ $\Rightarrow$ $α$p = ($α$ + 2p)$β$ ....(vi)

$β$ $-$ 3$γ$)p = 2$βγ$ $\Rightarrow$ 3$γ$p = (p - 2$γ$)$β$ .....(vii)

From (vi) and (vii),

$\frac{α}{3γ}=\frac{α+2p}{p-2γ}$

$\Rightarrow$ p$α$ - 6p$γ$ = 5$γα$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{p}{γ}-\frac{6p}{α}=5$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{p}{γ}+1=6\left (\frac{p}{α}+1\right )$ ....(viii)

Now from (v) and (viii),

$\frac{P(E_{1})}{P(E_{3})}$ = 6
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift

text: The maximum value of z in the following equation $z = 6xy + y^{2}$, where 3x + 4y $\leq$ 100 and 4x + 3y $\leq$ 75 for x $\geq$ 0 and y $\geq$ 0 is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
[IMG]


3x + 4y $\leq$ 100

4x + 3y $\leq$ 75

x $\geq$ 0, y $\geq$ 0

Feasible region is shown in the graph

Let maximum value of $6xy + y^{2} = c$

For a solution with feasible region,

$6xy + y^{2} = c$ and 4x + 3y = 75 must have at least one positive solution.

$y^{2}+6y\left (\frac{75-3y}{4}\right )-c=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{7}{2}y^{2}-\frac{225}{2}y+c=0$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{225}{2}\right )^{2}\geq 4.\frac{7}{2}.c$

$\Rightarrow c\leq \frac{225^{2}}{56}\approx 904$

text:
If [ . ] represents the greatest integer function, then the value of 

$\left |\int\limits _{0}^{\sqrt{\frac{π}{2}}}\left [[x^{2}]-\cos x\right ]dx\right |$ is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{0}^{\sqrt{\frac{π}{2}}}\left [[x^{2}]-\cos x\right ]dx$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{1}[-\cos x]dx+\int\limits _{1}^{\sqrt{\frac{π}{2}}}[1-\cos x]dx$

= $\int\limits _{0}^{1}[-\cos x]dx+\int\limits _{1}^{\sqrt{\frac{π}{2}}}1dx+\int\limits _{1}^{\sqrt{\frac{π}{2}}}[-\cos x]dx$

When 0 $\leq$ x $\leq$ 1 then -1 $\leq$ -cosx $\leq$ 0

$\therefore$ $[-\cos x]$ = -1

When 1 $\leq$ x $\leq$ $\sqrt{\frac{π}{2}}$ = 1.24 then -0.33 $\leq$ -cosx $\leq$ 0

$\therefore$ $[-\cos x]$ = -1 (Integer value present in the left side of -0.33)

$=-\int\limits _{0}^{1}dx+\int\limits _{1}^{\sqrt{\frac{π}{2}}}dx-\int\limits _{1}^{\sqrt{\frac{π}{2}}}dx$

$=-(x)_{0}^{1}=-1$

$\therefore$ $\left |\int\limits _{0}^{\sqrt{\frac{π}{2}}}\left [[x^{2}]-\cos x\right ]dx\right |$ = 1
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift

text: If the function $f(x)=\frac{\cos (\sin x)-\cos x}{x^{4}}$ is continuous at each point in its domain and $f(0)=\frac{1}{k}$, then k is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0}f(x)=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\cos (\sin x)-\cos x}{x^{4}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{k}=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{2\sin \left (\frac{\sin x+x}{2}\right )\sin \left (\frac{x-\sin x}{2}\right )}{x^{4}}$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{2\sin \left (\frac{x+\sin x}{2}\right )}{\left (\frac{x+\sin x}{2}\right )}\times \frac{\sin \left (\frac{x-\sin x}{2}\right )}{\left (\frac{x-\sin x}{2}\right )}\times \frac{x^{2}-\sin ^{2}x}{4x^{4}}$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}2\times 1\times \left (\frac{x+\sin x}{x}\right )\left (\frac{x-\sin x}{x^{3}}\right )\times \frac{1}{4}$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}2\times 1\times \left (\frac{1+\cos x}{1}\right )\left (\frac{1-\cos x}{3x^{2}}\right )\times \frac{1}{4}$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}2\times 1\times \left (\frac{1+1}{1}\right )\left (\frac{1-\cos x}{3x^{2}}\right )\times \frac{1}{4}$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}2\times 1\times \left (\frac{1+1}{1}\right )\left (\frac{1+\sin x}{6x}\right )\times \frac{1}{4}$

= $2\times 2\times \frac{1}{6}\times \frac{1}{4}$ = $\frac{1}{6}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift
